subject: Science
question: In coastal areas during the NIGHT-TIME, cool breeze blowing from the land towards the sea is called:
explanation: At night, land cools faster than the sea, so air over warmer ocean rises and cool land air flows seaward as Land Breeze.

It makes the mercury flow faster
It prevents the thermometer from breaking
explanation: The capillary kink introduces mechanical surface tension resistance, preserving the peak mercury reading.

question: Why should a clinical thermometer NEVER be washed or sterilized in boiling hot water?

Because hot water turns mercury into water
Because boiling water erases the painted numbers

question: Why are digital thermometers rapidly replacing traditional mercury glass thermometers in clinics and homes?

Mercury has stopped being manufactured worldwide
Digital thermometers are made of pure gold

subject: Science
question: Why do we prefer to wear light-colored or white clothes in hot summer and dark/black clothes in cold winter?

White clothes are lighter in physical weight
Dark clothes produce their own electricity

subject: Science
question: Why does wearing TWO thin woolen sweaters keep us significantly WARMER in winter than wearing one single thick woolen sweater of equal thickness?

Two sweaters create friction that generates fire
Two sweaters weigh twice as much
One thick sweater attracts cold radiation

question: Why are cooking utensils (like frying pans) made of metals like aluminium or stainless steel, but their handles are made of bakelite plastic or wood?

Because plastic is too heavy to make pans

subject: Science
question: When heating water in a round-bottom flask, why does water at the bottom rise to the top while cold water from the sides moves downwards?
options: Heated water expands, becomes less dense (lighter), and rises; cooler, denser water from sides sinks to replace it, setting up Convection Currents

subject: Science

Because laboratory thermometers only work under water

subject: Science
question: Why do houses in hot tropical climates have their outer walls painted WHITE or light pastel colors?

subject: Science
question: Why do rooms have electric room heaters placed on the floor and air-conditioners installed near the ceiling?

To keep AC out of reach of children
Because heaters look better on floors
Because ceilings are always hotter than floors
explanation: Optimized convective atmospheric circulation: dense chilled air descends while buoyant warm air ascends.

subject: Science
question: Why does a metal chair feel much COLDER to touch than a wooden table in the same room during cold winter mornings?

The metal chair is actually at a lower temperature than the wooden table
Wood produces its own internal heat
Metal absorbs cold from the floor
explanation: Both objects are at thermal equilibrium; metal feels colder due to its high thermal effusivity rapidly conducting hand heat away.

subject: Science
question: How does a double-walled thermos flask keep hot tea hot and cold water cold for hours?

It contains an internal battery heater
It is made of thick lead
explanation: Dewar flask design eliminates conduction/convection via evacuating interstitial air and halts radiation via reflective silvering.

subject: Science
question: What happens when you hold one hand above a burning candle flame and one hand on the side of the flame?
options: The hand above the flame feels much hotter because air above is heated by CONVECTION currents rising upward; the side hand feels only mild radiation
Both hands feel exactly the same heat
explanation: Thermal buoyancy channels convective heat plumes vertically above the flame; lateral heat transfer occurs solely by radiation.

subject: Science
question: What is the relationship between Celsius (°C) and Fahrenheit (°F) temperature scales?
explanation: Linear thermometric conversion equation: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32.

subject: Science
question: Why does wool fiber provide superior thermal warmth in winter garments?

subject: Science
question: What is 'Thermal Equilibrium' between two contacting bodies?
options: The state where both bodies reach the exact same temperature, resulting in zero net transfer of heat energy between them
When one body freezes the other
When heat doubles in both bodies
explanation: Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics: thermal equilibrium is attained when thermodynamic temperature gradient equals zero (dT/dx = 0).

All wax drops melt simultaneously at the exact same second

Heat will flow from iron ball to water
Heat will flow from water to iron ball
The temperature of both will increase to 80°C

question: Why do birds fluff up their feathers during freezing winter mornings?

To make themselves look bigger to predators
Because feathers become heavier in cold

question: Consider four identical metal blocks (Copper, Aluminium, Iron, Lead) of equal mass heated to 100°C and placed on a slab of ice. Which block melts the most ice?

All four melt the exact same amount of ice

subject: Science
question: Why does the greenhouse effect trap heat inside a glass greenhouse or parked closed car in the sun?

Glass produces heat from carbon dioxide
Because glass turns sunlight into hot water

options: The ONLY sea in the world that has NO land boundaries/shores, bounded entirely by four ocean currents forming the North Atlantic Gyre
An underground sea inside a cavern
A frozen sea in the Sahara Desert
explanation: The Sargasso Sea is defined exclusively by ocean current gyres (Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Current, Canary Current, North Equatorial Current).

subject: GK
chapter: Chapter 3: World Geography, Continents, Oceans & Famous Global Landmarks
question: What profound planetary perspective is revealed through the comprehensive study of World Geography and Landmarks?
options: Earth is a dynamic, interconnected planetary biosphere where physical plate tectonics, atmospheric currents, oceanic gyres, and cultural human civilizations form an interdependent global tapestry
Continents are fixed and never change over billions of years
All countries have identical climates and landforms
Human civilization developed independently of geographic rivers and resources
explanation: World Geography unifies geomorphic planetary dynamics with anthropogenic cultural adaptations across diverse biomes.

subject: Social Science
question: Under the rule of which Rajput dynasty did the city of Delhi first become the capital of a kingdom in the 12th century?
options: Tomara Rajputs (later defeated by Chauhans / Chahamanas of Ajmer)
explanation: Delhi first became a capital under the Tomara Rajputs, who were subsequently defeated by the Chauhans of Ajmer.

subject: Social Science
question: What were the commercial coins minted in Delhi that had a wide circulation across medieval trade routes called?
explanation: Coins minted in medieval Delhi were widely recognized as 'Dehliwal'.

subject: Social Science
question: What is the historical term for Persian histories/chronicles written by literate secretaries, administrators, and poets in the Delhi Sultanate?
explanation: Tarikh/Tawarikh were court histories written in Persian, the official administrative language of the Delhi Sultanate.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was the FIRST and ONLY female Muslim monarch to sit on the throne of the Delhi Sultanate (daughter of Sultan Iltutmish) in 1236 CE?
explanation: Raziyya Sultan ruled from 1236 to 1240 CE as recognized by chronicler Minhaj-i Siraj.

subject: Social Science
question: What was a fortified settlement with soldiers stationed permanently for military defense in the Delhi Sultanate called?
explanation: A garrison town was a heavily fortified urban military base garrisoned with soldiers.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the land adjacent to a city or port that supplied it with essential goods, agricultural produce, and services called?
explanation: The hinterland is the surrounding rural territory supplying resources, grain, and labor to an urban center.

subject: Social Science
question: What were the special military slaves purchased for military service and trained with great care by early Delhi Sultans (especially Iltutmish) called in Persian?
explanation: 'Bandagan' (plural of banda) were elite military slaves trusted by Sultans over hereditary aristocrats.

subject: Social Science
question: What was a territorial revenue assignment (land territory) granted to military commanders by the Sultans called?
explanation: An 'Iqta' was a provincial revenue tract assigned to commanders (Iqtadars/Muqtis).

subject: Social Science
question: What were the military governors or holders of an Iqta land assignment called?
explanation: Iqtadars (or Muqtis) governed Iqtas, maintaining soldiers and collecting territorial revenues.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the agricultural land tax levied on peasant produce, accounting for about 50% of the peasant's crop yield under Alauddin Khalji?
explanation: Kharaj was the standard 50% agricultural crop tax levied directly on cultivators.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was the notorious Central Asian Mongol conqueror whose forces invaded Transoxiana in 1219 and repeatedly attacked the Delhi Sultanate?
explanation: Genghis Khan unified the Mongols, invading Khwarizm and pressing against the northwest frontiers of India.

subject: Social Science
question: Which Moroccan traveler arrived in India during the 14th-century reign of Sultan Muhammad Tughluq and left an invaluable travelogue (Rihla)?
explanation: Ibn Battuta from Tangier, Morocco, served as Qazi of Delhi under Muhammad Tughluq and documented Sultanate governance.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the 'Circle of Justice' (Fakhr-i Mudabbir, 13th century) that explained the interdependent relationship between the King, soldiers, peasants, and state revenue?
options: A king cannot survive without soldiers -> Soldiers cannot live without salaries -> Salaries come from revenue collected from peasants -> Peasants can pay revenue only when they are prosperous and happy -> This happens when the king promotes justice and honest governance
A circle drawn on the ground for duels
A round table where judges sit
A magic circle protecting Delhi forts
explanation: The Circle of Justice (Daira-i Adalat) linked monarchical survival directly to peasant prosperity and judicial equity.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did the 13th-century chronicler Minhaj-i Siraj acknowledge that Raziyya was more able and qualified than all her brothers, yet felt uncomfortable with her rule?
options: He believed that female sovereignty violated the patriarchal ideal social order ordained by God, where women were supposed to be subordinate to men
Because Raziyya could not read Persian
Because Raziyya gave all kingdom wealth to foreign traders
explanation: Minhaj articulated medieval patriarchal ideology: viewing female monarchs as disrupting divine gender hierarchies.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did early Delhi Sultans (like Iltutmish) prefer to appoint their purchased military slaves (Bandagan) to high governorships rather than traditional noble aristocrats?
options: Slaves had no family lineage or hereditary local loyalties; they were entirely dependent on the Sultan for their livelihood and were exceptionally loyal and obedient
Because noble aristocrats could not fight wars
explanation: Royal patronage of Bandagan secured a dedicated praetorian corps personally beholden to the Sultan alone.

subject: Social Science
question: How did Alauddin Khalji maintain strict control over his Muqtis (Iqtadars) to prevent corruption and rebellion?
options: Their offices were made non-hereditary, Iqtas were assigned for short periods before frequent transfers, and state accountants were appointed to audit revenues and verify troop numbers
He let Muqtis keep all taxes without auditing
He gave Muqtis absolute permanent ownership of lands
explanation: Alauddin enforced non-hereditary tenure, frequent transfers, and rigorous auditing of Muqti revenue and troop contingents.

subject: Social Science
question: What market and price control measures did Alauddin Khalji implement in Delhi to maintain a large standing army at sustainable costs against Mongol invasions?
options: He strictly fixed the maximum selling prices of all commodities (grains, cloth, sugar, horses), appointed market inspectors (Shahna-i Mandi), and harshly punished any merchant who cheated or overcharged
He doubled the price of all foods
He banned all private markets completely
explanation: Alauddin's economic reforms: price caps, state grain silos, and market superintendents (Shahna-i Mandi) to sustain military mobilization.

subject: Social Science
question: What was Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq's infamous 'Token Currency' experiment and why did it fail disastrously?
options: He issued cheap copper and brass coins having the same face value as silver Tankas; people easily forged the simple copper coins at home, paid taxes in fake tokens, and hoarded genuine gold and silver coins
Because people threw coins into the river
Because the coins had no numbers written on them
explanation: Unminted token brass/copper tokens were easily counterfeited by artisans, bankrupting the imperial exchequer (Gresham's Law).

subject: Social Science
question: What was Muhammad bin Tughluq's controversial decision to shift the imperial capital from Delhi to DAULATABAD (Devagiri in Deccan)?
options: He wanted to govern southern peninsular India and defend against northern Mongol attacks more effectively, but forced the entire population of Delhi to march 1,500 km south, causing immense suffering
Because Delhi ran out of drinking water
Because he wanted to move to Europe
explanation: The forced relocation to Daulatabad (1327 CE) caused widespread fatalities during the transit and was subsequently abandoned.

subject: Social Science
question: In mosque architecture, what is the orientation towards Mecca that Indian Muslims face during prayer (towards the West) called?
explanation: Qibla is the sacred directional orientation toward the Kaaba in Mecca (due West from the Indian subcontinent).

subject: Social Science
question: What was the Friday congregational sermon delivered by the Imam during Namaz called?
explanation: The Khutba is the formal liturgical address and sermon delivered during Friday Juma congregational prayers.

subject: Social Science
question: What were the five distinct ruling dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in chronological order (1206 to 1526 CE)?
options: Early Turkish / Mamluk Slave Dynasty -> Khalji Dynasty -> Tughluq Dynasty -> Sayyid Dynasty -> Lodi Dynasty
explanation: Chronological sequence: Mamluks (1206–1290) → Khaljis (1290–1320) → Tughluqs (1320–1414) → Sayyids (1414–1451) → Lodis (1451–1526).

subject: Social Science
question: Which ambitious Afghan ruler defeated Mughal Emperor Humayun in 1540 and established the Sur Empire, creating an administrative model later adopted by Emperor Akbar?
explanation: Sher Shah Suri (r. 1540–1545 CE) standardized silver Rupiya currency, built the Grand Trunk Road, and designed administrative revenue systems.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the massive congregational mosque built by the Delhi Sultans in their first city (Dehli-i Kuhna) called?
options: Quwwat al-Islam Mosque and Qutb Minar complex
explanation: Quwwat al-Islam mosque and Qutb Minar were initiated by Qutbuddin Aibak and expanded by Iltutmish and Alauddin Khalji.

subject: Social Science
question: Who was the military general under Alauddin Khalji who led sensational military campaigns deep into South India (Warangal, Dwarasamudra, Madurai)?
explanation: Malik Kafur commanded Alauddin's southern military expeditions between 1309 and 1311 CE, extracting vast tribute in elephants and gold.

subject: Social Science
question: What new military garrison city was constructed by Alauddin Khalji for his soldiers in Delhi?
explanation: Siri was established by Alauddin Khalji c. 1303 as a heavily fortified military garrison town in Delhi.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the primary language of administration and official court record-keeping throughout the Delhi Sultanate?
explanation: Persian was the elite court language and bureaucratic administrative medium of the Delhi Sultanate.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did author Ziauddin Barani criticize Sultan Muhammad Tughluq for appointing wine distillers, barbers, cooks, and gardeners to high administrative posts?
options: Barani reflected aristocratic elite bias and lamented the loss of aristocratic monopoly over state power to low-born individuals
Because the appointees could not cook well
Because the appointees were foreigners from England
Because they refused to accept salaries
explanation: Barani's conservative aristocratic perspective decried merit-based or non-noble appointments as a decline of imperial judgment.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): Control of garrison towns in distant Bengal and Sindh from Delhi was exceptionally fragile and prone to frequent rebellion during the 13th century.
Reason (R): Communication routes were frequently severed by inclement monsoon weather, immense overland distances, and persistent rebellion by local governors and Mongol raids across the northwest frontier.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Pre-modern logistics and regional distances severely compromised the central authority of Delhi over outlying frontier garrisons.

subject: Social Science
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the comparative administrative strategies between Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq:
Group:
1. Alauddin Khalji built a new garrison town named Siri for his soldiers.
2. Muhammad bin Tughluq emptied the oldest city of Delhi (Dehli-i Kuhna) and moved residents to Daulatabad.
3. Alauddin Khalji paid soldiers in cash and strictly controlled market prices.
4. Muhammad bin Tughluq used pure diamond coins as common currency.
options: Statement 4 (Muhammad Tughluq used cheap TOKEN COPPER/BRASS coins, NOT diamond coins)
explanation: Statement 4 is an absurdity: Muhammad Tughluq experimented with base metal (bronze/copper) token currency, not diamond coins.

subject: Social Science
question:
Analyze the fiscal mechanics of the 'Iqta System':
How did the Sultanate ensure that Muqtis did not oppress peasants or hoard surplus state funds?
options: Muqtis were allowed to collect ONLY the taxes assessed by the state and maintain strictly prescribed contingents of soldiers; imperial accountants (Amils) audited tax records annually
Muqtis could take 100% of all village property
explanation: The state separated fiscal assessment from tax collection, deploying imperial accountants to check Muqti ledgers and muster rolls (Dagh and Chehra).

subject: Social Science
question:
Match Column I (Sultanate Dynasties) with Column II (Prominent Rulers / Timeline):
(a) Mamluk / Early Turkish (1206-1290) -> (i) Qutbuddin Aibak, Iltutmish, Raziyya, Balban
(b) Khalji Dynasty (1290-1320)         -> (ii) Jalaluddin and Alauddin Khalji
(c) Tughluq Dynasty (1320-1414)        -> (iii) Ghiyasuddin, Muhammad bin Tughluq, Firuz Shah
(d) Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526)           -> (iv) Bahlul, Sikandar, and Ibrahim Lodi
explanation: Exact chronological matching of the ruling dynasties and foundational sultans of Delhi.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the statements regarding military expansion of the Delhi Sultanate:
Statement 1: 'Internal Frontier' campaigns aimed at consolidating the hinterlands of the garrison towns by clearing forests in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab and settling peasant agriculture.
Statement 2: 'External Frontier' campaigns targeted military raids into Southern India to capture war booty, elephants, horses, and slaves.
Statement 3: The Delhi Sultans conquered and annexed the entire continent of Europe.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is historically false. Statements 1 and 2 represent the classic dual-axis military expansion model of the Sultanate.

subject: Social Science
question: Why was the Battle of Panipat (1526 CE) a watershed turning point in Indian history?
options: Babur (Mughal ruler of Kabul) defeated Ibrahim Lodi (last Sultan of Delhi), ending the 320-year Delhi Sultanate and founding the Mughal Empire
It established British rule in India
It ended all wars in Asia forever
It resulted in the partition of India
explanation: First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526): Babur's matchlocks and field artillery annihilated Ibrahim Lodi's forces, inaugurating the Mughal era.

subject: Social Science
question: How did Queen Rudramadevi (1262–1289 CE) of the Kakatiya dynasty of Warangal navigate patriarchal prejudices compared to Raziyya Sultan?
options: She changed her name on her royal inscriptions to pretend she was a man, adopting male persona to avoid social resistance to female kingship
She surrendered her throne to the Delhi Sultan
She banned all men from her kingdom
explanation: Rudramadevi adopted the masculine title 'Rudradeva Maharaja' on epigraphs to bypass patriarchal prejudices.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the significance of 'Begumpuri Mosque' built in the reign of Muhammad Tughluq?
options: It was the main congregational mosque of Jahanpanah, the 'Sanctuary of the World', Sultan Muhammad Tughluq's new capital in Delhi
It was built entirely of wood
It was built by the British
explanation: Begumpuri Mosque was the monumental central congregational Jami mosque of Jahanpanah, Tughluq's fourth medieval city of Delhi.

subject: Social Science
question:
Consider four key administrative elements introduced under Alauddin Khalji:
1. Direct state assessment of land revenue
2. 'Dagh' (branding of horses) and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll of soldiers)
3. Shahna-i Mandi (market superintendents)
4. Kharaj fixed at 50% of produce
What was the common primary strategic objective behind all four measures?
options: To maximize imperial revenue extraction and maintain a massive, highly efficient, standing military machine capable of crushing Mongol invasions
To encourage foreign merchants to take over the empire
To prepare for a pilgrimage to Mecca
explanation: All four reforms formed an integrated fiscal-military apparatus designed to sustain standing armies against continuous Mongol invasions.

subject: Social Science
question: What was the social background of the authors of Tawarikh (Persian histories)?
options: Learned urban men (secretaries, administrators, poets, courtiers) who lived in cities (mainly Delhi) and hardly ever in rural villages, writing histories to earn rich rewards from Sultans
Poor peasant farmers in remote villages
explanation: Tawarikh chroniclers were urban court literati dependent on royal patronage, articulating aristocratic perspectives.

subject: Social Science
question: Why did Ibn Battuta describe the fortress-like bamboo groves in India as impenetrable fortifications for local chieftains?
options: Giant interlocking bamboo clumps were dense, tough, and fire-resistant; chieftains lived securely inside them with their cattle and crops, cut off from cavalry attacks
Because bamboos were made of iron
Because wild tigers guarded the bamboos
explanation: Ibn Battuta documented how dense indigenous bamboo thickets formed natural defensive bastions impenetrable to imperial cavalry.

subject: Social Science
question: What master historical transformation is traced in Chapter 3 of NCERT Class 7 History regarding Delhi?
options: The transformation of Delhi from a minor regional Rajput trade post into the monumental imperial capital of a pan-subcontinental sultanate, creating new models of administrative centralization, fiscal taxation, and Indo-Islamic architectural grandeur
The complete abandonment of Delhi as a ruined ghost town
The conquest of Delhi by Roman emperors
The conversion of Delhi into a farming village
explanation: Chapter 3 chronicles the political, architectural, and fiscal institutional evolution of Delhi into an imperial metropolis.

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: एक या एक से अधिक वर्णों के मेल से बने सार्थक एवं स्वतंत्र ध्वनि-समूह को व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: वर्णों के सार्थक, व्यवस्थित और स्वतंत्र समूह को 'शब्द' कहते हैं (जैसे: कमल, पुस्तक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी व्याकरण में शब्दों का वर्गीकरण मुख्य रूप से कितने आधारों पर किया जाता है?
options: चार आधारों पर (1. उत्पत्ति / स्रोत के आधार पर, 2. रचना / बनावट के आधार पर, 3. अर्थ के आधार पर, 4. प्रयोग / विकार के आधार पर)
explanation: शब्दों का वर्गीकरण 4 आधारों पर होता है: उत्पत्ति (स्रोत), व्युत्पत्ति (रचना), अर्थ तथा रूप-परिवर्तन (प्रयोग)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संस्कृत भाषा के वे मूल शब्द जो बिना किसी परिवर्तन के अपने मूल रूप में हिंदी में ज्यों के त्यों प्रयुक्त होते हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: तत्सम शब्द (जैसे: अग्नि, सूर्य, दुग्ध, रात्रि, मयूर)
explanation: तत् + सम (उसके समान): संस्कृत के अविकृत मूल शब्द 'तत्सम' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संस्कृत भाषा के वे शब्द जो समय के साथ प्राकृत और अपभ्रंश से रूप बदलकर (परिवर्तित होकर) हिंदी में आए हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: तद्भव शब्द (जैसे: आग, सूरज, दूध, रात, मोर)
explanation: तत् + भव (उससे उत्पन्न): संस्कृत से रूप परिवर्तित होकर आए शब्द 'तद्भव' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वे शब्द जो स्थानीय बोलियों और जनसाधारण की आवश्यकतानुसार भारत के विभिन्न क्षेत्रीय परिवेश में विकसित हुए हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: देशज शब्द (जैसे: लोटा, पगड़ी, खिड़की, डिबिया, खटिया)
explanation: देश में ही जनभाषा के प्रभाव से उत्पन्न देशी शब्द 'देशज' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: विदेशी भाषाओं (अंग्रेज़ी, अरबी, फ़ारसी, पुर्तगाली, तुर्की) से संपर्क के कारण हिंदी में आए शब्दों को क्या कहते हैं?
options: विदेशी / आगत शब्द (जैसे: स्कूल, डॉक्टर, किताब, अखबार, साबुन, कैंची)
explanation: अन्य विदेशी भाषाओं से हिंदी शब्दकोश में समाहित शब्द 'आगत/विदेशी' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: रचना (बनावट) के आधार पर शब्द के कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: तीन भेद (1. रूढ़ शब्द, 2. यौगिक शब्द, 3. योगरूढ़ शब्द)
explanation: व्युत्पत्ति/रचना के 3 भेद हैं: रूढ़ (अखंड), यौगिक (संयुक्त) तथा योगरूढ़ (विशिष्ट अर्थ में रूढ़)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वे मूल शब्द जिनके सार्थक टुकड़े (खंड) नहीं किए जा सकते और जो किसी विशेष अर्थ में परंपरा से प्रसिद्ध हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: रूढ़ शब्द (जैसे: घर, जल, हाथी, पेड़, नाक)
explanation: जिन शब्दों के खंड निरर्थक होते हैं, वे 'रूढ़ शब्द' कहलाते हैं (घ + र का कोई स्वतंत्र अर्थ नहीं)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: दो या दो से अधिक सार्थक शब्दों या शब्दांशों के योग से बनने वाले शब्द क्या कहलाते हैं?
options: यौगिक शब्द (जैसे: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय, देव + दूत = देवदूत)
explanation: सार्थक खंडों के योग से बने नए शब्द 'यौगिक शब्द' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वे यौगिक शब्द जो अपने सामान्य अर्थ को छोड़कर किसी विशेष अर्थ (विशिष्ट रूढ़ अर्थ) के लिए प्रसिद्ध हो जाते हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: योगरूढ़ शब्द (जैसे: पंकज = कीचड़ में जन्मा कमल, दशानन = रावण, लंबोदर = गणेश)
explanation: यौगिक होकर भी किसी रूढ़ लाक्षणिक अर्थ को प्रकट करने वाले शब्द 'योगरूढ़' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: प्रयोग / व्याकरणिक प्रकार्य (विकार) के आधार पर शब्द के मुख्य रूप से दो भेद कौन-से होते हैं?
options: विकारी शब्द (Mutable) और अविकारी शब्द (Immutable / अव्यय)
explanation: व्याकरणिक विकार के 2 भेद हैं: विकारी (संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया) और अविकारी/अव्यय।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन शब्दों का रूप लिंग, वचन, कारक और काल के प्रभाव से बदल जाता है (परिवर्तित होता है), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: विकारी शब्द (जैसे: लड़का, लड़के, लड़कों ; पढ़ता है, पढ़ती है)
explanation: लिंग, वचन, कारक के अनुसार रूपांतरित होने वाले शब्द 'विकारी' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन शब्दों के रूप में लिंग, वचन, कारक या काल के कारण कभी कोई परिवर्तन नहीं होता (सदा एक समान रहते हैं), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: अविकारी शब्द / अव्यय (जैसे: धीरे-धीरे, और, किंतु, परंतु, अचानक, शाबाश)
explanation: न व्यय इति अव्यय: जो कभी रूपांतरित न हों, वे 'अविकारी / अव्यय' कहलाते हैं (क्रियाविशेषण, समुच्चयबोधक, संबंधबोधक, विस्मयादिबोधक, निपात)।

subject: Hindi Grammar

explanation: संस्कृत तत्सम 'अक्षि' का तद्भव रूपांतरण 'आँख' है।

explanation: संस्कृत तत्सम 'दुग्ध' का तद्भव रूप 'दूध' है।

question: तत्सम शब्द 'कर्ण' का तद्भव रूप क्या होगा?

question: तत्सम शब्द 'घृत' का तद्भव रूप क्या होगा?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: दो भिन्न भाषाओं के शब्दों के मेल से बने नवीन शब्द को व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
options: संकर शब्द (Hybrid Words : जैसे - रेलगाड़ी [अंग्रेज़ी+हिंदी], टिकटघर [अंग्रेज़ी+हिंदी], वर्षगाँठ [संस्कृत+हिंदी])
explanation: दो भिन्न भाषाई स्रोतों से निर्मित द्वैत-भाषी शब्द 'संकर शब्द' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: विकारी शब्द के अंतर्गत कौन-से चार व्याकरणिक भेद आते हैं?
explanation: चारों विकारी कोटियाँ हैं: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण और क्रिया।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अविकारी (अव्यय) शब्द के अंतर्गत कौन-से चार मुख्य भेद आते हैं?
explanation: अव्यय के 4 प्रमुख भेद: क्रियाविशेषण, संबंधबोधक, समुच्चयबोधक, विस्मयादिबोधक (तथा निपात)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अर्थ के आधार पर जिन शब्दों का एक निश्चित अर्थ निकलता है, उन्हें 'सार्थक' कहते हैं ; जबकि जिनका कोई स्वतंत्र अर्थ नहीं होता (जैसे: पानी-वानी, चाय-वाय, रोटी-वोटी में 'वानी, वाय, वोटी') उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: जिन ध्वनियों का कोई स्वतंत्र शब्दकोशीय अर्थ नहीं होता, वे बोलचाल के 'निरर्थक शब्द' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: समान अर्थ प्रकट करने वाले भिन्न-भिन्न शब्दों (जैसे: सूर्य = रवि, भानु, दिनकर, भास्कर) को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: समान अर्थ वाले पर्यायवाची (समानार्थी) शब्द कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: परस्पर विपरीत (उल्टा) अर्थ प्रकट करने वाले शब्दों (जैसे: सत्य - असत्य, अमृत - विष, अनुराग - विराग) को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: विपरीत भाव/अर्थ देने वाले शब्द 'विलोम' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन शब्दों के एक से अधिक अर्थ होते हैं (जैसे: 'कर' = हाथ, टैक्स, किरण, सूंड), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: प्रसंगानुसार भिन्न-भिन्न अर्थ देने वाले शब्द 'अनेकार्थी शब्द' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जो शब्द सुनने और पढ़ने में लगभग एक समान लगते हैं परन्तु उनके अर्थ में भारी अंतर होता है (जैसे: 'अनल' = आग और 'अनिल' = वायु), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: समान ध्वन्यात्मक आभास वाले भिन्न अर्थी शब्द 'श्रुतिसम भिन्नार्थक' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'दशानन' (दस आननों वाला) शब्द किस वर्ग का शब्द है?
options: योगरूढ़ शब्द (क्योंकि इसका विशेष रूढ़ अर्थ 'रावण' के लिए निश्चित हो चुका है)
explanation: दश + आनन यौगिक होकर रावण के लिए विशेष अर्थ में निश्चित होने से 'योगरूढ़' है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: पुर्तगाली भाषा से हिंदी में आए शब्दों का सही युग्म कौन-सा है?
explanation: पुर्तगाली व्यापारियों से हिंदी में आए शब्द: आलू, बाल्टी, साबुन, तौलिया, चाबी, आलमारी, गमला।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: तुर्की भाषा से हिंदी में आए प्रमुख शब्दों का सही समूह कौन-सा है?
explanation: तुर्की मूल के शब्द: कैंची, तोप, बारूद, बेगम, तलाश, चाकू, बहादुर।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'शब्द' और 'पद' में तात्विक अंतर होता है — शब्द कोश की स्वतंत्र सत्ता है, जबकि पद वाक्य में व्याकरणिक नियमों में बँधा रूप है।
कारण (R): जब 'कमल' स्वतंत्र लिखा जाता है तो वह शब्द है, परन्तु जब 'कमल खिलता है' लिखा जाता है तो 'कमल' कारक-विभक्ति और लिंग-वचन से युक्त होकर 'पद' बन जाता है।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: शब्द स्वतंत्र भाषिक इकाई है; वाक्य में प्रयुक्त होकर रूपात्मक संबंध प्राप्त करने पर वह 'पद' बन जाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: श्रुतिसम भिन्नार्थक शब्दों 'कुल' और 'कूल' का क्रमशः शुद्ध अर्थ क्या है?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: श्रुतिसम भिन्नार्थक शब्दों 'गृह' और 'ग्रह' का क्रमशः सही अर्थ क्या है?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अनेकार्थी शब्द 'कनक' के तीन प्रमुख संदर्भगत अर्थ क्या हैं?
explanation: 'कनक कनक ते सौगुनी...' कनक के प्रमुख अर्थ: स्वर्ण (सोना), धतूरा और गेहूँ हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अनेकार्थी शब्द 'अंबर' के दो मुख्य अर्थ क्या हैं?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: योगरूढ़ शब्दों में कौन-सा समास विशेष रूप से अंतर्निहित होता है?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:

'छायादार' शब्द किन दो भिन्न भाषाओं के मेल से बना है?

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: शब्द विचार (Morphology) के विशद अध्ययन का भाषा प्रयोग में क्या केंद्रीय निष्कर्ष है?

विदेशी शब्दों का प्रयोग पूरी तरह बंद होना चाहिए
